search.scope: complete repository working tree at the classified revision, excluding .git
search.method: the registered Rust oracle recursively scans the repository root for Model/Transaction schema literals, persisted Model digest/reference spellings, exact-codec or versioned-envelope producer tokens, and same-line lower-hex-64 literals with Model/Transaction language; only .git, the generated directory names `target`, `node_modules`, `dist`, and `__pycache__`, the two trees in `excluded_trees`, and the two exact files in `excluded_paths` are excluded
search.definition: a Model-bearing fixture is a checked-in file that carries Model artifact bytes, a Model artifact digest, or an assertion pinning a Model artifact identity; search hits that are product surfaces or source/package identities are classified but are not promoted into the identity-delta class
search.excluded_paths_note: this case excludes exactly two executable files: the integration-test root and the private transition-contract module it includes with `#[path]`, split because a single file exceeded the 2,000-line test ceiling. Both spell the tokens the sweep searches for, so both are excluded by exact path — never by their directory, by a suffix rule, or by anything resembling `crates/*/tests/`. The adjacent admission and later-classification regression modules deliberately carry no searched signal and remain visible to the sweep. Every other test file in the repository, including the sibling oracle `crates/eqiora-artifact/tests/current_model_wire_oracle.rs`, stays a classified candidate; any additional executor that carries a searched signal arrives as an unclassified candidate and is returned to this oracle.

transition.contract: the epoch reset is an exact two-state transition, not a sentinel heuristic. Every inventory path is either retired or preserved; `retired` additionally names the staged control-v2 promotion sources and the retired control-v1 request fixtures, which carry no search signal and are therefore not inventory members.
transition.pre_reset: every path in `retired` exists, every inventory path exists, the discovered candidate set equals the frozen inventory exactly, every promotion source carries its frozen sha256, no promotion target marked `target_exists_pre_reset: false` exists yet, and no path in `required_post_reset_without_frozen_bytes`, `post_reset_admitted`, `post_reset_fixture_admitted`, or `post_reset_classified` exists yet
transition.post_reset: no path in `retired` exists, every preserved inventory path exists although an in-place migration may stop matching the search signal, every path in `required_post_reset` exists — those in `promotion` carrying their frozen sha256, those in `required_post_reset_without_frozen_bytes` by existence alone — every path in `preserved_evidence` exists, every declared product-source scope is free of every forbidden token, every optional path in `post_reset_admitted`, `post_reset_fixture_admitted`, or `post_reset_classified` that exists carries exactly its recorded search-signal and identity-literal inventory, and the discovered candidate set is contained in the preserved inventory together with `required_post_reset`, `post_reset_admitted`, `post_reset_fixture_admitted`, and `post_reset_classified`
transition.partial_transition: any other combination fails, including exactly one retired path missing before the reset and exactly one retired path surviving after it. A proper nonempty subset of `retired` is never an admissible state, so a reset cannot land one seam at a time.
transition.unchanged_from_the_accepted_contract: no new signal-bearing path may appear in either state by inference; `required_post_reset` is the complete set of paths the reset is permitted to add, and of those only `schemas/control/compile-v2.schema.json`, the promoted historical v1 schema copy, the promoted historical cylinder resource, and the two unversioned Rust wire owners carry a search signal. A signal-bearing path created later, by work the reset did not do, enters only through an exact amendment to this frozen record: identity-free surfaces through `post_reset_admitted`, exact fixtures through `post_reset_fixture_admitted`, and mixed or source/package identity evidence through `post_reset_classified`. None is inferred by the state predicate, a glob, a directory, or proximity.
transition.escape: an implementation that needs another new signal-bearing path, another declared scope exclusion, or that cannot retire a listed path, stops and returns the delta to this oracle. Widening a set here to admit an implementation choice is not an available move.
transition.ownership_of_the_unversioned_wire_owners: the reset folds the retired `model_v8.rs` and `model_transaction_v8.rs` wrappers together with the surviving current encoding into `crates/eqiora-artifact/src/model_wire.rs` and `crates/eqiora-artifact/src/model_transaction_wire.rs`. This gives the exact current persisted wire an unversioned product owner without growing the already-large `model.rs` and `model_transaction.rs`. Their existence is required; their content is not frozen here, because this oracle does not own the current encoding — `artifacts.current-model-canonical-identity` does.
transition.counts: 44, 304 and 13 are not one partition of 338. What partitions the inventory is 34 + 304: the 34 retired paths that are inventory members plus the 304 preserved ones. The other 10 retired paths carry no search signal and were never members. The 13 required paths are post-reset additions and replacements, not inventory members: 12 are created by the reset, and `verify/interfaces/control-plane-compile-check/expected/contract.json` is the one existing member whose bytes are replaced in place. Of the 13, 11 carry a frozen promotion digest — 10 staged control-v2 sources plus the historical cylinder — and 2 are required by existence alone.

transition.preserved_evidence_note: invariant evidence only: every path here exists at the same location in both states. The historical Model and Transaction specimens survive as a negative rejection corpus, and no Realization, Run, spatial, or geometry family member is retired by this transition. Evidence whose location changes is not listed here — it is in `promoted_evidence`, so that both the real pre-reset state and the synthetic post-reset state stay exact rather than being the union of two phases.

promoted_evidence.note: the same bytes are evidence in both states at different paths, so it is preserved evidence in neither. Its pre-reset path is retired, its post-reset path is required, and the byte identity between them is the `promotion` entry.

transition.promoted_evidence_note: each entry names one evidence file whose bytes survive and whose owner changes. `pre_reset` is a member of `retired`, `post_reset` is a member of `required_post_reset`, and a `promotion` row freezes the exact bytes carried across. Deleting the bytes rather than moving them fails as a substituted promotion, not as a missing path.
transition.post_reset_admitted_contract: an identity-free classified path created after the reset is admitted by exact path and by nothing else. Admission is containment-only: it adds the path to what the post-reset discovered set may contain and never requires the path to exist, so a post-reset state carrying none of the admitted paths is accepted exactly as it was before this amendment. An admitted path that does exist must carry exactly the search signals recorded for it and must freeze no Model-derived lower-hex-64 identity literal; an admitted path present in the pre-reset state is refused as mid-flight, because admission describes a path the reset did not create and the pre-reset tree did not have.
transition.post_reset_admitted_is_not_membership: no admitted path joins `inventory`, `retired`, `retired_outside_inventory`, `required_post_reset`, `required_post_reset_without_frozen_bytes`, `preserved_evidence`, `promoted_evidence`, or any `promotion` row, and no count above moves. Listing one in the inventory would claim it existed before the reset; listing one in `required_post_reset` would claim the reset created it and would make a later capability mandatory for acceptance. Both are false.

forbidden_product_tokens.why: path existence cannot see a private historical branch left inside a file the reset preserves. `encode_v1`--`encode_v8` and `ensure_v1`--`ensure_v8` live today in `crates/eqiora-artifact/src/model.rs`, `model_transaction.rs`, `model/node.rs`, `model/expression.rs`, and `model/vocabulary.rs`, every one of which survives the reset. A contract that only counted paths would call that reset complete.
forbidden_product_tokens.matching: exact case-sensitive byte substring over UTF-8 file content. No regular expression, no language parser, and no `#[cfg(test)]` stripping: a permissive textual parser would decide what a scope contains by guessing, which is what this contract exists to avoid.
forbidden_product_tokens.not_scanned: verify fixtures, oracles, and the control-v2 contract and schema falsifiers; `crates/*/tests/`; `bindings/python/tests/`; `rfcs/`; `docs/`; `CHANGELOG.md`; `schemas/`; and every retained artifact byte. Those hold the negative corpus and the historical record the reset must keep, and forbidding a token there would delete the evidence that the reset happened.
forbidden_product_tokens.pre_reset_non_claim: this contract is never evaluated against the pre-reset checkout: it carries almost everything the reset removes, and refusing it would be refusing the state this case ships in. `pre_reset_occurrence` records exactly how much of it is there, because "the tree spells all 102" would be false.

pre_reset_occurrence.why: a post-reset-only token contract is worth nothing if the tokens were never there to remove, so non-vacuity has to be measured rather than asserted. It is measured exactly: 98 of the 102 tokens occur in the files their own scope covers, and 4 do not.
pre_reset_occurrence.measured_over: the checked-in files each scope covers in this pre-reset checkout, by the same exact case-sensitive substring rule the post-reset scan uses
pre_reset_occurrence.prospective: the four absent tokens are prospective post-reset guards, not observations. No product source spells them today; they name the per-generation entry points beside `from_program_v3`--`from_program_v8`, `from_json_v3`--`from_json_v8`, `from_transaction_v3`--`from_transaction_v8`, and `digest_v3`--`digest_v8`, which is where a renamed historical v2 branch would most plausibly reappear while the reset is being written. Forbidding them after the reset costs nothing and catches that; claiming they occur now would be false.
pre_reset_occurrence.post_reset_claim: unchanged. After the reset all 102 tokens are forbidden in every declared scope, present ones and prospective ones alike.

classes.mixed-claim-surface: one file contains claims with different semantic fates; each claim has its own selector, class, and disposition. classes.compatibility-only: sole claim is that a removed Model or Transaction generation stays callable or byte-stable; deleted by the reset

classes.prose-transcript: documentation transcript of one flat compilation; unreproducible by construction and covered by no registered case

classes.non-fixture-search-hit: a product declaration or consumer surface found by the exhaustive candidate sweep; it migrates in place but contributes no frozen identity literal

dispositions.delete: the path is retired and its sole claim goes with it
dispositions.rename-source: the path is retired and the behaviour it hosts moves unchanged to the unversioned owner named in `renames_to`
dispositions.delegate: another registered case owns the claim; this case neither freezes nor migrates it, whatever happens to the path itself under `search.transition`
dispositions.migrate: the path survives and its claim moves to the current owner, with any identity literal it carries substituted by the precommitted successor
dispositions.preserve-bytes: the path survives byte-identical, and any Model reference inside it stays opaque
dispositions.decompose-by-claim: the file carries several claims with different fates; each entry in `claims` carries its own disposition
dispositions.migrate-in-place: the path or claim survives in place and contributes no Model-derived identity transition here. Immutable source/package identities may remain byte-stable under this disposition. The identity-free inventory remainder inherits it, and only paths that survive may: no retired path is left to it.

disposition_completeness: every entry naming at least one path declares exactly one disposition from the vocabulary above, no path is named by two entries, and every one of the 338 inventory paths therefore has exactly one fate: 109 from an entry and 229 from the remainder rule.

entries.note: these two are retired paths and are not compatibility-only: they host the exact current persisted wire, which survives. RFC 0083 keeps `v8` in persisted names and makes the source owners unversioned, so the reset moves the behaviour to `model_wire.rs` and `model_transaction_wire.rs` and removes the version-named paths. Calling that a deletion would misstate what happens to the encoding; leaving it to the remainder would call a removed path an in-place migration. The mapping is per file, not per set: Model goes to `model_wire.rs` and Transaction to `model_transaction_wire.rs`, and `renames` states that pairing so a swap is a failure rather than a re-ordering. The content of the new owners is not frozen here — `artifacts.current-model-canonical-identity` owns it — so `search.transition` requires them by existence alone.

every candidate path in classification-inventory.txt not named by an entry above is a product declaration, consumer, test harness, or documentation search hit; it receives no identity literal and remains subject to current-owner migration rather than deletion. The rule excludes retired paths by construction: all 34 retired inventory members are named by an entry above — 15 as compatibility-only deletions, 2 as version-named current owners the reset renames, 2 as the v2-named source files decomposed by claim because they host the current v8 implementation, and 15 by the fixture, delegated, and remaining mixed-claim entries — so no path this remainder covers is one the reset removes.
